fact: The document states that Togo has a 2024-2028 National Cybersecurity Strategy, which the ANCy call for a national expert pool supports.
The National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCy) is stated to operate, issuing a call for expressions of interest dated 27 August 2026 to build a national pool of cyber experts.
CERT.tg is described as Togo's national centre for responding to cybersecurity incidents, with a mission of detection, prevention and response.
CERT.tg issued a public alert on a surge of compromises of WhatsApp, Facebook and other online accounts in Togo; the article dates it to Thursday 20 August 2026 (inferred from its publication date).
CERT.tg is stated to be Togo's national cybersecurity incident response center, run by Cyber Defense Africa, which was set up in 2019 by the Togolese government and Asseco Data Systems.

The article states the national incident response centre CERT.tg was created and that ANCy is the national cybersecurity agency; no creation date is given, so the publication date of 2025-11-03 is used.
The article cites a national cybersecurity strategy 2024-2028 among Togo's cybersecurity initiatives; no adoption date is given, so the publication date of 2025-11-03 is used.
The document refers to Togo's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCy) as operating, running a nationwide awareness tour with its second stage at Elavagnon on 9 September 2026.
The National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCy) is stated to be running, since 7 September 2026, the second phase of a national cybersecurity training programme for 350 public-administration staff.
The National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCy) is stated to have held the fourth stage of its national awareness tour at Kougnohou on 14 September 2026, for nearly 200 attendees.
ECOWAS states Cyber Defense Africa is the operator of Togo's national Computer Emergency Response Team, CERT.tg, which hosted a SIM3 auditor training in Lomé on 4 to 6 August 2026.
ANCy issued a high-severity alert on an active account-compromise campaign hitting WhatsApp, Facebook and other services, urging two-factor verification.
The document describes ANCy as the national cybersecurity agency issuing alerts to users.
ANCy is reported to have recorded and handled 333,000 incidents over 2021-2024, rising from 39,168 in 2021 to 181,088 in 2024.
ANCy is stated to have recorded and handled 333,000 incidents between 2021 and 2024.
ANCy is described as the national agency with permanent monitoring and rapid response operating.
ANCy director-general Gbota Gwaliba is quoted giving more than 333,000 incidents handled between 2021 and 2024.
More than 333,000 incidents were handled between 2021 and 2024, per ANCy's director-general.
ANCy is named as the national cybersecurity agency headed by a director-general; document published 2026-07-21 gives no creation date.
Article 6 of law 2018-026 creates the Agence nationale de la cybersécurité (ANCy), national authority for essential infrastructure security, with an alert and response structure attached.
The deck lists the Cybersecurity Act of 2018 as creating a Cybersecurity Agency.
Togo's national cybersecurity agency ANCy presented the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2024-2028, with four pillars, to some 300 stakeholders in Lome.

CERT.tg, the Centre National de Réponse aux Incidents de Cybersécurité, issued public alert 202504/AP/09 on 27 April 2025 about a phishing campaign using a fake free-data offer in the names of Yas Togo and Moov Africa Togo.
The Agence Nationale de la Cybersecurite (ANCy) issued a public alert on 3 December 2024 warning of a fake 45,000 XOF Christmas subsidy scam, and offers CERT.tg incident assistance.
